tool.name: SIMORGH
tool.description: Deep learning framework for apo-state and cryptic pocket prediction
tool.command: ln -s '$pdb' input.pdb #if str($bbflow_condi.bbflow) == 'yes': && bbflow_sample --input_path input.pdb --output_path bbflow.pdb --output_format pdb --num_samples $bbflow_condi.num_samples #if str($bbflow_condi.batch_size) != '': --batch_size $bbflow_condi.batch_size #end if --device cpu --timesteps $bbflow_condi.timesteps --tag $bbflow_condi.advanced.tag #if str($bbflow_condi.advanced.gamma_trans) != '': --gamma_trans $bbflow_condi.advanced.gamma_trans #end if #if str($bbflow_condi.advanced.gamma_rots) != '': --gamma_rots $bbflow_condi.advanced.gamma_rots #end if && python /opt/SIMORGH/Model/realign.py -i bbflow.pdb -o bbflow_aligned.pdb #end if && python /opt/SIMORGH/Model/inference.py #if str($bbflow_condi.bbflow) == 'yes': -i bbflow_aligned.pdb #else -i input.pdb #end if -o predicted.pdb --model1 /opt/SIMORGH/Model/model_4.pt --model2 /opt/SIMORGH/Model/model_44.pt #if str($cluster_condi.cluster) == 'yes': --cluster --cutoff $cluster_condi.cutoff --min-cluster-size $cluster_condi.min_cluster_size --min-samples $cluster_condi.min_samples --alpha $cluster_condi.alpha #end if

tool.help:
What it does -------------
SIMORGH predicts apo-state and cryptic ligand-binding sites from a single protein structure. Given an input PDB file, it outputs a residue-level predicted probability of ligand binding for each residue, using two trained models — a geometric encoder and an ensemble aggregator — and writes the predictions to an output PDB file.
Apo-state structures lack ligand-induced pocket organization, which poses a bigger challenge for pocket prediction. This challenge is more pronounced for cryptic pockets. To address this, we can optionally generate an ensemble of alternative backbone conformations using BBflow, capturing greater conformational heterogeneity and improving sensitivity to pockets not visible in the input structure.
Predicted site scores can also optionally be clustered using HDBSCAN — useful when you want to detect multiple binding sites separately and remove the noise, rather than just a general per-residue probability map.
Inputs -------
* **PDB file**: the input protein structure to analyze.
* **Run BBflow?**: if enabled, samples alternative backbone conformations of the input structure before prediction.
* **Number of conformations to sample**: how many backbone conformations BBflow generates. * **Number of sampling timesteps**: number of integration steps used by the BBflow sampler; more timesteps can improve sample quality at the cost of runtime. * **Batch size**: number of conformations sampled per batch; left blank, it is estimated automatically. * **Advanced prior parameters (gamma_trans / gamma_rots)**: control how closely the sampling prior sticks to the input (equilibrium) structure. Left blank, the values from the model's training configuration are used.
* **Run Clustering on predictions?**: if enabled, groups predicted site points into clusters using HDBSCAN.
* **Probability cutoff for clustering**: minimum predicted probability for a point to be considered when forming clusters. * **HDBSCAN min_cluster_size**: minimum number of points required to form a cluster. * **HDBSCAN min_samples**: HDBSCAN density parameter; higher values yield more conservative (less noisy) clustering. * **Probability weight in custom distance metric**: weight given to the predicted probability, relative to spatial distance, when computing the distance metric used for clustering.
Outputs --------
* **Predicted Structure**: the input structure (or the BBflow-sampled conformation, if BBflow was run) annotated with predicted binding-site scores in b-factor column. * **BBflow Structure**: only produced if BBflow sampling was enabled; the backbone conformations sampled by BBflow prior to prediction.
